capabilities.text: Launch the tool from a custom button embedded in the Epic EHR navigation menu for the current patient
Automatically retrieve and display the most recent clinical note for the patient from Epic via the FHIR API
Allow nurses to review and edit the retrieved clinical note in a clean, editable text field
Save the edited note to a designated SharePoint Online worksheet using the SharePoint REST API
Include metadata with each saved note such as timestamp, nurse ID, and patient ID
Enforce role-based access control restricting tool usage to nurses in the Azure AD group for Ward 4B
Show a visible success confirmation message after a note is successfully saved to SharePoint
Handle save failures by keeping the edited text in the editor, showing an error message, and automatically retrying once after 10 seconds
Provide a manual Retry button after a failed automatic retry to allow nurses to attempt saving again
Block saving of empty or whitespace-only notes and prompt nurses to enter text before saving
Allow nurses to cancel editing and close the tool without saving changes, discarding any edits
Disable the Save button and show a message if the SharePoint worksheet is unreachable at tool startup
Hide the Epic launch button for users not in the authorized Ward 4B Azure AD group
Display clear error messages and deny access if a user outside the authorized group attempts to access the tool directly
Display an error and disable saving if the patient context (MRN or encounter ID) is missing when launching the tool
Log all save attempts, successes, failures, and retries with nurse ID, timestamp, patient context, and HTTP status codes in Azure Monitor
Use a minimal REST API with two endpoints: one to retrieve the latest note and one to save the edited note, secured with Azure AD bearer tokens
Deploy the tool as a single-page web app served from an Azure Function App behind API Management with throttling to handle up to 30 requests per minute
Display a clear UI disclaimer that edits made in the tool do not update the original note in Epic, which remains the source of truth
